clue.text: Orchestra catch up around start of joyful chorus

parts.note: the Hallé is a famous Manchester orchestra

indicators.note: the reversed catch goes around the next letter, enclosing it
in a down clue, up means the word is read bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: a haul is a catch, as of fish

indicators.note: start of means only the first letter of joyful is taken

parts.note: first letter J

explanation.surface: An orchestra rushes to catch up with a choir launching into a joyful chorus.
explanation.walkthrough: HAUL turned upwards gives LUAH, which wraps round J to make LUJAH; the Hallé, a Manchester orchestra, goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hallelujah Chorus from Handel's Messiah is so famous that the single word names that choral piece.

clue.text: Lots of holes in this wood perhaps

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a ..., the organisation, has a course of many holes
second meaning: a wood is one kind of club used to hit a golf ball

explanation.walkthrough: One sense is the members' club owning an eighteen-hole course; the other is the stick, of which a wood is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a sporting society with its course and the implement a golfer swings, such as a driver.

clue.text: Tax collecting? It's fun!

indicators.note: the tax word gathers up the next piece inside itself

parts.note: a levy is a tax
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wry question about whether gathering taxes could ever be enjoyable.
explanation.walkthrough: LEVY takes in IT, giving LEV-IT-Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Levity is light-hearted humour or frivolity, close in sense to merriment.

clue.text: Mass inspires fashionable man on board

indicators.note: to inspire is to breathe in, so the mass letters take the next piece inside

parts.note: KG, kilogram, is a unit of mass
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: A church Mass motivates a trendy man aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' looks like a church service but is KG, the kilogram; 'on board' means a chessboard, not a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The king is a piece in chess, a man being the old term for any piece on the board.

clue.text: Working out goalie's job, one appearing in paper

parts.note: a goalkeeper's job is keeping goal

indicators.note: the number one shows up inside the paper's letters

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times newspaper
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A goalkeeper who exercises turns up in the newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper; I goes inside to make FIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing exercise to stay healthy is keeping fit, as working out at a gym is.

clue.text: Solve Times cryptic crossword, initially at home?

parts.note: to do a puzzle is to solve it

indicators.note: cryptic means hidden or puzzling, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of crossword

parts.note: first letter C

explanation.surface: A question whether one tackles the Times cryptic crossword at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cryptic' reads as describing the crossword, but it is the signal to rearrange TIMES.
explanation.definitionFit: Domestic describes things belonging to the household, so it fits life within one's own house, with a question mark for the stretch.

clue.text: A posh couple's foreign 6?

definitions.note: 6 down is DOMESTIC, so a domestic helper from abroad

parts.note: U means upper-class, posh
a pair is a couple

explanation.surface: An upper-class pair employs a foreign servant.
explanation.walkthrough: The 6 refers to 6 down, DOMESTIC, used as a noun for a household servant.
explanation.definitionFit: An au pair is a young person from abroad who helps with housework and childcare in exchange for lodging.

clue.text: Help plan last first

indicators.note: the last letter is moved to the front of the word

parts.note: an idea is a plan

explanation.surface: An instruction to aid a plan by putting the final stage first.
explanation.walkthrough: IDEA with its final A brought to the front gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An aide is an assistant, the person who gives help, as help can mean a helper.

clue.text: Make good magazine earlier

parts.note: to atone is to make amends, make good
Time is an American news magazine

explanation.surface: An instruction to repair a magazine from the past.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means formerly, in the past, so it can stand for previously.

clue.text: One inspects pupils losing way round Windows

indicators.note: losing means the way letters drop out

parts.note: an oculist is an eye doctor, examining pupils of the eye
ST is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: A school inspector misplaces the route around Microsoft Windows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pupils' seem schoolchildren but are eye parts; 'Windows' seems the software but means architectural windows.
explanation.definitionFit: Oculi are circular openings in architecture, such as the eye at the top of a dome.

clue.text: Giving a boost to Jack's function

definitions.meaning: first meaning: raising up or encouraging
second meaning: a car jack's job is raising the vehicle

explanation.walkthrough: Jack looks like a man's name but is the tool for raising a car.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising something both boosts it and is exactly what a jack does to a vehicle.

clue.text: Top cleric's scripture class fills course

indicators.note: the class letters go inside the course word, filling it

parts.note: a plate of food is a course of a meal
RE, religious education, is the school subject

explanation.surface: A senior churchman's bible lesson fills a period of study.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is religious education in British schools; course is a dish, not a study programme.
explanation.definitionFit: A prelate is a high-ranking churchman such as a bishop or archbishop.

clue.text: Either half of sweetbread

parts.note: split the word as sweet and bread; the answer means each half: a lollipop and slang for cash

explanation.walkthrough: Sweetbread is an offal dish, but split in two its halves are a sweet (an ice lolly or lollipop) and bread, British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a lollipop treat and, in British slang, money, which bread also means.

clue.text: Bare contents of French well, by the sound of it

indicators.note: signals that the French phrase is spoken and the answer is what it sounds like

parts.note: a French well holds eau naturelle, natural water

explanation.surface: Plain description of what a French well holds, judging from how it sounds.
explanation.walkthrough: EAU, French for water, sounds like AU, and naturelle sounds like NATUREL.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means naked or in a natural state, so it is a jokey word for nude.

clue.text: I see a scavenger going round creating flyers

indicators.note: the scavenger goes round the I and C, enclosing them

parts.note: a vulture is a scavenging bird
taken as written
the letter C sounds like see

explanation.surface: Someone watches a scavenger circling, as if conjuring birds into the air.
explanation.walkthrough: VULTURE wrapped round IC gives VICULTURE; A goes before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Aviculture is the breeding and keeping of birds, which produces more winged creatures.

clue.text: Brown maybe settles on skip

definitions.note: Capability Brown, the 18th-century English garden designer

parts.note: to land is to settle or come to rest
a caper is a playful skip or leap

explanation.surface: A brown bird perhaps alights on a skip, the large rubbish container.
explanation.walkthrough: Brown is Capability Brown, England's famous landscape gardener; 'skip' looks like a rubbish bin but is a hop.
explanation.definitionFit: Capability Brown designed grand parkland estates, an example of a garden designer.

clue.text: Mad Bojo is in fact admitting day's a reward for work?

indicators.note: the jumbled letters let in the day
mad means crazy, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the fodder
SAT is short for Saturday

explanation.surface: A jibe that crazy Boris Johnson's governing is really a reward for his efforts.
explanation.walkthrough: Bojo is a nickname for Boris Johnson, the former British prime minister; the day is slotted into the jumbled letters after the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Contentment from one's employment is an intangible return for doing a job well, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Current noble's relations

parts.note: AC is alternating current
a count is a nobleman; count's gives the letters with S

explanation.surface: An aristocrat's relatives are present-day ones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relations' looks like family but means narratives.
explanation.definitionFit: Accounts are reports or narratives, as relations are tellings of events.

clue.text: River Test's vigour

parts.note: the Indus is a river in Pakistan
a try is a test or attempt

explanation.surface: The River Test, in Hampshire, flows energetically.
explanation.walkthrough: The Test is a real English river, but here test simply means try.
explanation.definitionFit: Industry can mean diligent energy and hard work, close to vigour.

clue.text: Silk may be found in this elevated part of Wimbledon

definitions.text: Silk may be found in this

parts.note: high means raised, elevated
Wimbledon tennis is played on courts

explanation.surface: Silk fabric discovered in a raised section of the Wimbledon tennis venue.
explanation.walkthrough: A silk is a senior British barrister (a King's Counsel, who wears a silk gown).
explanation.definitionFit: Senior barristers argue cases in the High Court, the superior civil court of England and Wales.

clue.text: Information about a way to tidy beds

indicators.note: the information word goes about the other letters

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
RD is short for road, a way

explanation.surface: Tips on a method for keeping flower beds neat.
explanation.walkthrough: Gen is British informal for information.
explanation.definitionFit: To garden is to tend plants and keep flower beds weeded and orderly.

clue.text: Special day for old Roman teams

parts.note: the Ides was a date in the ancient Roman calendar

explanation.surface: A festival day for the teams of ancient Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: Sides are opposing groups of players in a game, as teams are.

clue.text: Analyst's quiet place for bowling

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
a rink is the stretch of green where bowls is played

explanation.surface: A psychoanalyst's calm bowling alley.
explanation.walkthrough: A rink is a lane on a bowling green, as used in lawn bowls.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrink is slang for a psychiatrist, short for headshrinker.

clue.text: Mostly clean quarterdeck for hobby?

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: pure means clean
a suit is a quarter of a deck of cards

explanation.surface: Is scrubbing most of a ship's quarterdeck a pastime?
explanation.walkthrough: The quarterdeck is a ship's deck, but read as quarter deck it is one of the four suits in a pack of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A pursuit is an activity one follows for pleasure, a pastime.

clue.text: One's often driven in job

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a stake or fence ... hammered into the ground
second meaning: a position of employment

explanation.walkthrough: Driven sounds like a car but means hammered.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a stake knocked into earth and an appointment or position of employment.

clue.text: Server's first to stop backing horse

indicators.note: the first letters stop up the reversed horse, going inside it
backing means the horse word is reversed

parts.note: an Arab is a breed of horse
1ST, written IST, means first

explanation.surface: A waiter is first in line to stop betting on a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: ARAB backwards is BARA; 1ST, read with I for 1, goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A barista makes and serves coffee in a café, a kind of waiter.

clue.text: Tied up by strapping American

indicators.note: strapping means binding round, so the by letters are wrapped about the next piece

explanation.surface: Someone bound by a burly American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strapping' looks like an adjective meaning brawny, but it is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Being tied up idiomatically means occupied, engaged with work.

clue.text: Liquid waste, a by-product of hard labour

definitions.meaning: first meaning: perspiration is fluid the body excretes
second meaning: perspiration, or toil itself

explanation.walkthrough: Both halves point to the same word from different angles: what the body excretes and what heavy effort produces.
explanation.definitionFit: Perspiration is a bodily fluid excreted through the skin and appears with heavy exertion.

clue.text: Eg Central Park race is about to block country bumpkin there

indicators.note: the reversed letters block the bumpkin word by sitting in it

parts.note: rube is American slang for a country bumpkin; there points to the US setting of Central Park

indicators.note: about means the race and is pieces turn round

parts.note: to run is to race

explanation.surface: In New York's Central Park, a runner obstructs a rustic yokel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'country bumpkin' alone suggests HICK or YOKEL; 'there' tells you to use the American word, since Central Park is in New York.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means the country in the city, describing a large urban park like New York's.
